messages:
Alex (Sales): Heads-up — PulseCart (Dedicated dp-82) just reported checkout failures. They measured p95 ~220ms -> ~710ms and overall throughput fell ~50% since 2025-04-02T14:30Z. Req sample id=fc3d21. They said the issue started right after our morning edge rollout.
Priya (Support): Ticket #8022 created. Customer attached Console traces showing large queue depths on gpu-node-27 and model fallback events. They said payments are timing out for some shoppers.
Diego (PM): What's the contract on dp-82? Any committed burst or QPS guarantees? This looks like a P0 for them if checkout fails. @Tasha @Omar can you triage and propose rollback vs targeted mitigation?
Tasha (Eng): Pulling logs now. Which route are they hitting? Any client-side retry spikes?
Priya (Support): Route POST /v1/generate -> route id r-9b2f. Customer notes they pinned model to `redwood-xlarge-v2`. Console shows automatic fallback to `redwood-large-quant` around the time of the surge.
Omar (Infra): CI deploy pushed routing/batching tuning at 14:25 UTC (deploy-bot: deploy/2025-04-02). Node metrics show queue depth on gpu-node-27 rising from 0.2 -> 3.1 around 14:28.
deploy-bot: deploy/2025-04-02 finished: routing-tuning.
Tasha (Eng): Logs excerpt:
2025-04-02T14:30:12Z WARN batching: effective_batch_n lowered 8->2 route=r-9b2f pool=dp-82
2025-04-02T14:30:13Z ERROR serve: queue_wait=1.12s model=redwood-xlarge-v2 req=fc3d21
2025-04-02T14:30:14Z INFO routing: switched to redwood-large-quant for req=fc3d21 (fallback due to capacity)
Tasha (Eng): Hypothesis: the new batching thresholds are shrinking batches for this route which increases per-request overhead; fallback to quantized variant then triggers extra decode overhead and cache churn. Combined effect = p95 spike + throughput collapse.
Alex (Sales): PulseCart demanded immediate fix. Can we pin them to their preferred model and bump their pool burst for now? They asked for a written ETA.
Diego (PM): Agreed to emergency mitigation. Action: 1) temporarily pin dp-82 traffic to `redwood-xlarge-v2` and disable cross-tenant batching changes for that pool; 2) allocate short-term burst capacity for dp-82 while we stabilize; 3) open rollback if mitigation fails in 15m. Tasha leads. Omar handles pool capacity.
Tasha (Eng): Applying targeted override: route r-9b2f -> force model=redwood-xlarge-v2, set min_batch=6 for dp-82. Pushing change now.
Tasha (Eng): Override applied at 2025-04-02T14:35 UTC. Monitoring.
Tasha (Eng): Quick update: p95 reduced to ~240ms within 6 minutes, throughput nearing baseline. Queue depths dropped on gpu-node-27.
Priya (Support): PulseCart confirms checkout flow restored in their test environment, no errors observed. They want confirmation of root cause and whether this will reoccur.
Diego (PM): Next steps: immediate: keep overrides for 1hr while we evaluate. Short-term follow-up: revert or harden batching heuristics to avoid penalizing tenant-specific traffic. Product decision: add "per-tenant isolation" flags and an emergency safe-mode on the roadmap. Also, consider SLA credits for PulseCart if impact confirmed.
Alex (Sales): I'll notify the customer and offer credits if the postmortem confirms regression. Will ask for acceptance that the mitigation is acceptable.
Tasha (Eng): I'll file internal bug with attachment: logs, timeline, minimal repro and the canary config we applied. Tentative engineering fix: adjust heuristic to avoid reducing batch targets below route-specific historical minima and add a KV-cache warmup step when fallback model switches.
Omar (Infra): I'll open infra task to add queue-depth alerts with automatic escalation to routing safe-mode (reroute to pinned model or raise burst). Owner: Omar.
Diego (PM): Assign owners and priorities: eng-platform (P1) owner Tasha, infra (P1) owner Omar, product (P2) owner Diego for roadmap item "per-tenant safe-mode + burst controls".
Priya (Support): I'll leave ticket open and mark as monitoring. Customer said: "Thanks — flow is back, will let us know if they see regressions tomorrow morning." :thumbsup:
Tasha (Eng): I'll include the applied override configuration and rollback steps in the bug. If mitigation shows instability elsewhere, we'll rollback the routing-tuning release.
Diego (PM): We'll review scope and acceptance criteria for the per-tenant controls in next planning meeting; need rough estimates from Tasha/Omar for effort.
Alex (Sales): Customer asked to prioritize this into the next sprint if we can't give a long-term guarantee. Flagging potential escalation to contracts.
Diego (PM): Noted. We'll treat as roadmap candidate and discuss prioritization.
Priya (Support): Closing the active alert once PulseCart confirms stable for 45 minutes; leaving ticket for postmortem notes.
Tasha (Eng): Thanks all — reopening thread if we see regressions.
Omar (Infra): Adding playbook item for queue-based auto-escalation.
Diego (PM): Good work. I'll create backlog item "per-tenant isolation & emergency safe-mode" and link to the bug. Closing for now. :white_check_mark:
